passages.context: Printed pp. 170–173 (PDF pages 191–194) were visually inspected through the following-item boundary. Preisendanz presents PGM IV.3007–3086 as a distinct item directed toward persons described with daimon-language, with material, written, spoken, and adjuratory elements in alternating Greek text and German translation. This verifies the architecture and vocabulary of the 1928 edition only; it does not establish manuscript accuracy, dating of the item's composition, Jewish or Christian authorship, ordinary practice, efficacy, diagnosis, continuity, influence, or equivalence with Christian exorcism.
passages.notes: No ingredients, names, commands, formula, or procedural sequence is transcribed. The source remains a technical magical-text analogue, not an operational source; the revised Preisendanz edition, a manuscript facsimile, and a modern translation remain separate controls.
